transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-07-14
- Time: 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Maria Gonzalez (Acme), Tom Baker (Acme), Leah Chen (Acme), Eric Park (Acme)

Notes: call is weekly POC check-in #3 for the Acme Retail retrieval + rerank pilot. Recording/auto-transcript follows (auto transcript, may contain mishearings).

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Maria, Tom, Leah, Eric from Acme, and Priya and I from Redwood. Uh, agenda — results review, tuning last week, success criteria confirmation, and next steps.

[00:32] Maria Gonzalez: Yep, thanks Jordan. Quick context — we're close to the end of the three-week pilot, want to make sure perf looks good and that we can build a business case. Leah will cover evals.

[00:55] Leah Chen: Hi all. I ran the evals overnight, sent the spreadsheet earlier. High level — relevance improved by about 12% for the reranked results vs baseline, recall held steady. Some query classes still show regressions on really long-tail queries.

[01:20] Priya Raman: Got it, can you share an example of long-tail failures? sample queries?

[01:34] Leah Chen: Sure — product name misspellings and SKU-ish queries. I put a few rows in the sheet called "long_tail_cases". Also noted that for heavy session flows the latency p95 drifted up to ~820ms.

[01:55] Tom Baker: Yeah that p95 is the thing we've been watching. Baseline we get around 420ms with current infra, so doubling is concerning for UX.

[02:12] Priya Raman: That's helpful. The p95 increase we saw was during the non-batched path; on dedicated settings we can bring that down. We pushed a small kv-cache tweak this week which helped prefix hits by ~20%. Need to run with larger sequence lengths to reproduce.

[02:45] Eric Park: Quick question — what's the cost delta if we move to Dedicated? We need numbers for the exec deck.

[02:58] Jordan Lee: Short answer, Dedicated gives predictability but higher committed cost. I will send a detailed pricing sheet; rough math in pilot shows about 30% higher monthly committed cost versus pure hosted on our metering, but per-token unit cost for heavy traffic can be lower because of batching and caching.

[03:22] Maria Gonzalez: Also we need to confirm compliance — SOC2 details, VPC, KMS. Can Redwood provide artifacts?

[03:33] Jordan Lee: Yes — we'll share SOC2 summary and our VPC deployment checklist. Priya will follow up with the on-prem/private docs if you need air-gapped options.

[03:52] Leah Chen: Back to the metrics — I also computed cost per query from the pilot telemetry: hosted path average cost is $0.012 per query, with Dedicated projections around $0.009 if traffic sustained. But that assumes 70% cache hit and batching.

[04:18] Priya Raman: Exactly — caching and batching are the levers. We can propose tuning to improve prefix cache hit — we saw an immediate uplift after the kv tweak. Also consider quantization profile for the model which can reduce compute and latency; we tested int8-optimized variant with small quality delta.

[04:45] Tom Baker: Any regression risk with quantization? Leah, did you see quality drop in the evals?

[04:55] Leah Chen: Minimal on core queries, some edge cases worse. I flagged those. Can do a focused eval on the quantized config.

[05:12] Priya Raman: We'll run the quantized eval on your prompt set and return the confusion matrix. Expect run by Friday.

[05:30] Jordan Lee: Great. On the UX side, the product team wants p95 under 600ms for the majority of queries to feel snappy. Is that the right bar?

[05:40] Eric Park: Yes, that's the target. If we can get to ~500-550 consistently, we can present to execs.

[05:51] Maria Gonzalez: Also, success criteria for business case — Leah's relevance improvements plus cost-per-query under $0.01 with predictable capacity. If both boxes checked, we can move to procurement.

[06:05] Jordan Lee: Good — so success criteria draft: +10% relevance (relative), p95 < 600ms on production-like load, and projected cost per query <= $0.01 with Dedicated or caching strategy. We'll formalize and send.

[06:27] Tom Baker: For the production-like load, we should test at peak concurrent sessions — our telemetry peaks at 8k RPS during sale events.

[06:40] Priya Raman: Noted. We'll schedule a stress run at 10k RPS to give headroom. We'll also enable autoscale and capture tail latency.

[06:55] Leah Chen: One more item — rerank model sometimes pushes fewer diverse results for category queries; not sure if that's the model or prompt formulation. We tried a diversity penalty but haven't tuned it.

[07:10] Priya Raman: We can run a prompt-temp ablation and adjust sampling/penalty. That's low risk and quick.

[07:22] Jordan Lee: Ok timeline check — today is week 3, next week we aim to finish final benchmarks and have a short exec review the week after. Does that align with Acme internal timelines?

[07:35] Eric Park: Yes, we're aiming to present to finance/ops on the 22nd. Need cost and compliance artifacts by then.

[07:47] Maria Gonzalez: Procurement will need an SOW and pricing; Tom, can you coordinate once Jordan sends the proposal?

[07:56] Tom Baker: Yep will do.

[08:02] Jordan Lee: Cool. On the technical actions — Priya, you to run: kv-cache large sequence tests, quantized eval, and a 10k RPS stress test. Share logs and configs.

[08:16] Priya Raman: I'll also include kernel settings and batching logs. Note that we might recommend a small model variant or custom kernel for p95 improvements on Dedicated.

[08:30] Leah Chen: For the evals, I'll finalize the prompt set and label the edge cases; if you can run the quantized and non-quantized comparison that would be ideal.

[08:43] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Now questions from Acme?

[08:48] Maria Gonzalez: One last — what about data residency? We need EU data for EU customers. Is that supported?

[08:58] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can pin region routing and Dedicated pools in EU. For hosted we have EU regions; for Private we can do on-prem or VPC in-region. We'll include the regional deployment notes.

[09:12] Eric Park: Any blockers on our side? We need the final success criteria doc to sign.

[09:20] Jordan Lee: We'll draft the success criteria doc and share today. Also Jordan to send pricing. Priya to run benchmarks. Leah/Tom to finalize eval prompts. Maria to collect compliance questions.

[09:35] Maria Gonzalez: Sounds good. Can you confirm the timeline in writing?

[09:40] Jordan Lee: Yes — will share a follow-up email with action items and dates.

[09:47] Priya Raman: Quick note — we observed an anomaly in tokenization for certain SKUs that caused higher token counts; we'll share a patch and tokenizer config. Could affect cost calc slightly.

[10:02] Leah Chen: Thanks, that explains some cost variance.

[10:10] Jordan Lee: Alright, wrapping up. Recap of next steps and owners in the notes and action item list. Thanks everyone.

[10:20] Maria Gonzalez: Thanks all.

[10:25] Meeting ended.

References:
- Shared spreadsheet: https://redwood.example.com/sheets/acme-pilot-evals (shared earlier)
- Pilot telemetry dashboard link: https://console.redwood.example.com/dashboards/acme-pilot

Transcript end.
